Best linear unbiased predictions of the random effects

Source: R/estimates.R
vlm_blup.Rd

The predictions \(\widehat{\mathbf{u}} = \widehat{\mathbf{G}}\mathbf{Z}^{\top}\widehat{\mathbf{V}}^{-1} (\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}})\) of the random effects of a fitted model, with the standard errors of prediction \(\sqrt{\mathrm{diag}(\mathbf{C}_{22})}\), t tests and prediction limits: the solution for random effects of SAS PROC MIXED.

Usage

vlm_blup(fit, level = 0.95)

# Default S3 method
vlm_blup(fit, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fit

a result of vlm_fit().

level

confidence level of the prediction limits (default 0.95).

Value

A list of class c("vlm_blup", "vlm_result", "list") with blup (effect, subject, level, prediction, standard error of prediction, df, t, p and limits).

Details

For a single random factor with \(n_i\) observations on level \(i\), the prediction reduces to $$\widehat{s}_i = \frac{n_i\widehat{\sigma}_s^2}{n_i\widehat{\sigma}_s^2 + \widehat{\sigma}^2} (\bar{y}_{i\cdot} - \widehat{\mu}),$$ a shrinkage of the level mean towards the overall mean (Example 2.4.3.1 of the book). The degrees of freedom are the residual ones, or Satterthwaite ones (numerical derivatives of the prediction-error variance) with ddfm = "satterth" or "kr".

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi. Section 2.4.3.

Henderson, C. R. (1975). Best linear unbiased estimation and prediction under a selection model. Biometrics, 31, 423-447.

See also

vlm_fit

Other VetResearchLMM inference: emmeans_mixed_model(), report_mixed_model(), vlm_estimate(), vlm_lsmeans()

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

# Example 2.4.3.1: PROC MIXED; CLASS sire; MODEL ww = ; RANDOM sire / SOLUTION;
fs <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Ww ~ 1
    , data     = ex127
    , random   = ~ sire
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "default"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
bl <-
  vlm_blup(
      fit   = fs
    , level = 0.95
    )
bl
